title: Breathing in and out
examples: Where do my lungs help me breathe?
What happens when I breathe out?
Can you show me how to breathe deeply?

explain.say: Your lungs are like two soft balloons inside your chest.
Now look! Here it is in 3D: the lungs. Can you see the trachea and the bronchus? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.
When you breathe in, you take fresh air into your lungs.

draw.text: Breathe in: Fresh air enters lungs

explain.say: The fresh air in your lungs helps your body get the oxygen it needs.
When you breathe out, you push used air from your lungs.

draw.text: Breathe out: Used air leaves lungs

explain.say: When we breathe in and out, we keep our bodies working every day.
When you run and play, you breathe faster to get more air.

faq.q: Where does the air go when I breathe in?
faq.a: The air first goes through your nose or mouth, then down a tube called the trachea, and finally into your lungs.
asks: Where does the air travel to?

faq.q: What is the difference between breathing in and breathing out?
faq.a: Breathing in brings fresh air with oxygen to your body. Breathing out pushes out the used air.
asks: Is breathing in the same as breathing out?
What is the job of breathing out?

faq.q: Do I need to breathe when I sleep?
faq.a: Yes, you must breathe even when you are sleeping. Your body keeps needing oxygen all night long.
asks: Do I stop breathing at night?
Is breathing important when I sleep?

faq.q: Why do I breathe faster when I exercise?
faq.a: When you exercise, your muscles use more oxygen. So, you breathe faster to get enough fresh air.
asks: Why is breathing faster when running?
Does exercise make me breathe more?

faq.a: Yes, your lungs are always working to help you breathe. They work non-stop day and night.

facts: Your lungs are located inside your chest cavity.
Breathing in brings oxygen into your body.
Breathing out removes carbon dioxide from your body.
You breathe automatically without having to think about it.

quiz.say: When you breathe in, what gas do your lungs take in?
quiz.why: Oxygen is the fresh gas your body needs to live and move.

wrong.0: This is too general; oxygen is the specific gas needed.
wrong.2: This is the gas you breathe out, not in.
wrong.3: While air has nitrogen, your body needs oxygen most.

quiz.say: What is the main job of breathing out?
quiz.why: Breathing out gets rid of the used air, which has waste gas.

wrong.1: Getting oxygen happens when you breathe in.
wrong.2: This is a physical action, not the main purpose.
wrong.3: The goal is to empty the used air out.

quiz.say: If you are running very fast, how will your breathing change?
quiz.why: More activity means more oxygen is needed quickly.

wrong.1: This would mean you do not get enough air.
wrong.2: Your body needs more air when you are working hard.
wrong.3: You still use your nose when you are active.
